risks: Community Q4_K_M (72159246080 bytes, ~67.2GiB) is a derivative quantization: file SHA256, repo revision, license and GGUF architecture do not attest equality with unquantized official Leanstral 1.5 weights or tactic quality. Loading it on fent-reactor (two RTX 3090 24GiB, ~126GiB RAM, swap and a concurrent job) can breach the 16GiB host reserve, 48GiB RSS cap or 20GiB per-GPU cap. Full 119B fine-tuning stays disabled; DGX Spark memory is unavailable.

A healthy owned llama.cpp on localhost:18180, a sixteen-token rfl protocol smoke, a model-emitted verified flag, or a subprocess exit without proof records is not proof optimization. Historical port-8080 HTML is not a Leanstral endpoint. Silent truncation of the theorem statement, unfiltered retrieval, or a new Mathlib import on a Core-only pin can edit a different target. Environment or pin failures must not be labeled semantic negatives or model failures.

Unequal token or native-check budgets invalidate the original-proof, goal-state and retrieved-context ablation and the one-shot versus iterative-repair comparison. Local 3090 inference does not attest closed-track OpenRouter eligibility or open-track 4x80GiB A100 runtime. This review does not establish a shorter verified proof or a globally shortest proof.
actions: After native projects are ready, load only the pinned community Q4 artifact once size and SHA256 match, using owned isolated llama.cpp on localhost:18180: context 2048, batch 64, microbatch 32, at most 8 CPU threads, 18 GPU layers split across both cards, remainder in CPU RAM, cgroup limits, and stop only the owned service on a resource violation. Record health, advertised identity and memory before any generation. Keep the rfl smoke as its own record, separate from proof improvement.

Then run two requests, at most 1024 input plus 256 output tokens, 90s each and 240s total, comparing exact original-proof, goal-state and version-filtered import-scoped retrieved-context prompts. If a source does not fit, select authenticated spans or skip with a reason. Bind prompts to source bytes, target, prefix, toolchain, imports and pins. Repair loop: keep a verified incumbent, propose a bounded edit, feed back the actual compiler diagnostic, accept only an independently checked all-pin improvement, and compare with one-shot generation at matched budgets. Deduplicate by source and environment identity.

Preserve statement, binders, universes, target identity, imports, namespace and source prefix. Count helpers toward length. Reject sorry, admit, new axioms and unsafe escapes against the pin's permitted axiom set. Keep length-first, strict-dual and official-score reports separate. Record context tokens, deadlines, input/output tokens, latency, native-check cost, RSS and per-GPU memory, and accepted versus rejected edits. Stop at the 240s, two-request or memory guard; retain the incumbent and failures. Leave JLR-023 through JLR-025 and training unimplemented. Expand context only after a recorded memory and quality experiment.
acceptance_boundaries: This artifact is an advisory design review only. It does not execute Leanstral, Lean, Lake or an experiment, and it does not complete JLR-G005 runtime qualification. A route receipt for JLR-013 completes the design task. Actual tests and Lean compilation are separate evidence. Hypothesis under test later: bounded compiler-feedback prompts can be evaluated with frozen quantized Leanstral before any training.

Inference success, rfl output and native proof acceptance are three different outcomes. Fresh complete-source checks against exact Lean, Lake, dependency and source pins are the acceptance boundary. Environment failures stay infrastructure failures and never become proof failures or training labels. Executable-definition changes are outside this proof-only design and would need a separate checked equivalence plus runtime checks.

Stop at the task budget and record failures without inventing successful evidence. No finite frozen-model run establishes a globally shortest proof. Training, LoRA/QLoRA, model promotion, competition submission and Git push are out of scope.
